What is the Kings County Superior Court?

The Kings County Superior Court is a trial court located in the Central Valley of California. It is part of the California court system and is responsible for hearing cases in Kings County. The court has jurisdiction over both criminal and civil matters, including family law, juvenile cases, and probate matters.

History of the Kings County Superior Court

The Kings County Superior Court was established in 1893, shortly after Kings County was formed. The court originally held sessions in various locations throughout the county before finally settling in its current location in Hanford in 1940. Over the years, the court has undergone many changes, including the addition of new courtrooms and the implementation of new technology.

Types of Cases Heard in Kings County Superior Court

The Kings County Superior Court hears a wide variety of cases, including:

The court hears all types of criminal cases, including misdemeanors and felonies. The court also handles preliminary hearings and arraignments.

Civil Cases

The court handles civil cases, including contract disputes, personal injury claims, and other civil matters.

Family Law Cases

The court hears family law cases, including divorce, child custody, and child support cases.

Juvenile Cases

The court handles juvenile cases, including delinquency and dependency cases.

Probate Cases

The court handles probate matters, including wills, trusts, and estate disputes.

How the Kings County Superior Court Operates

The Kings County Superior Court operates like most other courts in California. It has a presiding judge, who is responsible for overseeing the court's operations. The court also has a number of judges and commissioners who hear cases and make rulings.
